name: QuantumScape
short_description: Pioneer of solid-state lithium-metal batteries for electric vehicles.
why_relevant: Public benchmark that showed solid-state can go from lab to vehicle progress.
history: QuantumScape was founded in 2010 by former Stanford researchers and quietly developed ceramic solid-state separators before going public in 2020 at a valuation near $10 billion. A strategic partnership with Volkswagen deepened through multi-year supply agreements and joint ventures. The company shipped its first low-volume A-samples in 2022, reached 24-layer cells, and unveiled its QSE-5 cells in late 2024, followed by B-samples in 2025. QSE-5's Cobra separator production, along with its Battery Elite program targeting EVs, keeps it on track toward commercial deployment.

name: Solid Power
short_description: Develops sulfide-based solid-state cells with automotive partnerships.
why_relevant: Brings solid-state chemistry onto standard Gigafactory production lines.
history: Solid Power spun out of the University of Colorado in 2012 to commercialize sulfide-based solid-state electrolytes. It raised private funding before going public in December 2021, then partnered with BMW and Ford on multi-year joint development agreements. The company scaled cells from 20 to 100 Ah, introduced dry-process electrodes, and licensed its electrolyte technology to SK On. In 2024 it delivered automotive-format A-2 cells for customer qualification and continued expanding its pilot line in Louisville to support mid-decade EV deployment.

name: 24M Technologies
short_description: Inventor of the semi-solid lithium-ion cell, the basis of the 3TO fabrication process.
why_relevant: Cuts battery capex and enables gigafactories with dry coating.
history: 24M Technologies was founded in 2010 out of MIT to redesign lithium-ion manufacturing with its semi-solid electrode, eliminating the drying step of conventional coating lines. Volkswagen's European funding helped scale the platform, and licensees such as Kyocera, Fujifilm and Thailand's GPSC brought the technology to Asia. In 2023 the company unveiled the 3TO process, a fully dry, continuous fabrication method, alongside its Eolify chemistry and cell technologies. It now licenses its platform to partners such as FREYR while pursuing direct production of long-duration and EV cells.

name: Lilac Solutions
short_description: Efficient ion-exchange process extracting lithium from brine.
why_relevant: Unlocks global brine resources without evaporation ponds.
history: Lilac Solutions was founded in 2016 to solve the slow, land-hungry problem of lithium-from-brine extraction using a reusable ion-exchange bead platform. It gained early support from Bill Gates' Breakthrough Energy Ventures and closed a $150 million Series B in 2022 among a crowded field chasing direct lithium extraction. Field pilots in Nevada, Argentina, Bolivia and the Salton Sea validated performance, and commercial agreements with developers such as Lake Resources and Vulcan Energy followed. The company is now scaling its modular plants to support multi-decade lithium supply contracts without evaporation ponds.

name: StoreDot
short_description: Develops extreme-fast-charging (XFC) silicon battery cells.
why_relevant: Silicon anode cells proven to charge from 10 to 80 percent in minutes.
history: StoreDot was founded in 2012 in Israel to develop extreme fast-charging (XFC) cells, shifting from lithium-ion work to silicon-dominant anodes that deliver meaningful range in minutes. Series D funding in 2021 included Daimler, BP and Samsung, and its '100in5' roadmap demonstrated charging 100 miles of range in five minutes. The company shipped B-samples to global OEMs such as Volvo and VinFast and announced commercial customer readiness. It continues metalloid-based chemistries and aims for '100in3' performance while licensing its XFC technology to battery partners.

name: Energy Dome
short_description: Makes a CO2-based long-duration storage battery from off-the-shelf components.
why_relevant: Cheap, abundant materials for a station-scale energy storage power plant.
history: Energy Dome was founded in 2017 in Milan by Claudio Spadacini and colleagues from the energy industry to commercialize a CO2-based long-duration battery built from off-the-shelf components. A first demonstrator in Sardinia began operating in 2022, and the company closed $55 million of funding led by investors including the European Innovation Council. Its 20 MWh Ottana plant validated the charging-discharging CO2 cycle, and the company signed baseline deals to deploy commercial units in regions such as Africa and Italy. Energy Dome remains focused on replacing gas peakers with cheap, scalable storage.

name: Highview Power
short_description: Operates liquid-air energy storage for multi-hour, mega-scale power.
why_relevant: Confirmed 2.5 GWh-hour-scale projects built from non-lithium materials.
history: Highview Power was founded in 2005 to develop liquid-air energy storage (LAES), building on a prototype at a Scottish power station. Its 5 MW/15 MWh Pilsworth plant near Manchester, commissioned in 2018, was the world's first grid-scale liquid-air system. The company raised strategic investment from GE, Sumitomo and Citigroup in the following years and secured planning consent for a 300 MWh facility at Carrington. In 2025 a consortium led by new investors recapitalized Highview to fund long-duration projects, with more gigawatt-scale LAES capacity planned in the UK.

name: Form Energy
short_description: Deploys multi-day iron-air batteries to replace gas peaker plants.
why_relevant: Proof that multi-day battery operation is possible at low cost.
history: Form Energy was founded in 2017 by a team including former Tesla executive Mateo Jaramillo to deliver cheaper multi-day storage using iron-air chemistry. The company raised over $1 billion from investors such as ArcelorMittal, Breakthrough Energy Ventures and TPG. In 2023 its first full-scale 1 MW/100 MWh battery was installed in Minnesota with Great River Energy, and in early 2024 it opened a high-volume iron-air plant in Weirton, West Virginia. Xcel Energy selected the company for a 10 MW/1 GWh project to replace natural-gas peakers.

name: Natron Energy
short_description: Manufactures sodium-ion batteries without lithium or cobalt.
why_relevant: Cycles 50,000 times with fire-safe chemistry for data centers.
history: Natron Energy was founded in 2012 to commercialize sodium-ion batteries using Prussian-blue electrodes, a chemistry free of lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese. Backed by investors including ABB and Chevron Technology Ventures, the company spent years optimizing cycling performance, achieving 50,000-cycle capability. In 2024 Natron began commercial production at a dedicated facility in Holland, Michigan, targeting data centers, UPS systems and industrial backup power that benefit from instant high-power output and inherent fire safety. The company is scaling further manufacturing capacity to serve expanding data-center demand.

name: EnerVenue
short_description: Builds metal-hydrogen Energy Storage Vessels for long-duration storage.
why_relevant: Decades of life and 75-year operation target from space-proven tech.
history: EnerVenue was founded in 2017 to adapt nickel-hydrogen chemistry proven in space missions for terrestrial long-duration storage, licensing technology developed at Stanford and NASA. A $100 million funding round in 2021, co-led by investors including Schlumberger New Energy, accelerated its Energy Storage Vessel (ESV) product. The company opened a high-volume manufacturing facility in New Richmond, Wisconsin, and began shipping its metal-hydrogen vessels, which target 30-year service with minimal degradation under daily cycling. EnerVenue is standardizing on large-format containers for renewable and utility applications.

name: Vulcan Energy
short_description: Produces lithium and renewable heat from geothermal brines in the Rhine Valley.
why_relevant: Zero-carbon lithium produced inside Europe to secure battery supply.
history: Vulcan Energy was founded in 2018 to combine geothermal power generation with lithium extraction from brines in Germany's Upper Rhine Valley, branding the approach Zero Carbon Lithium. It listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in 2020 and advanced exploration across a large licensed area, signing offtake agreements and equity partnerships with Stellantis, Renault and LG. In 2023 the company commissioned the Lithium Extraction Optimization Plant (LEOP) in Landau to prove commercial viability. It is now reaching final investment decisions on a central lithium plant powered by its renewable heat and power assets.

name: EnergyX
short_description: Developer of direct lithium extraction membranes and solid-state tech.
why_relevant: Commercial-scale brine production targeting the US critical minerals gap.
history: EnergyX was founded in 2018 by Teague Egan to develop direct lithium extraction membranes and solid-state technologies, addressing the growing US reliance on imported critical minerals. The company won validation through lab and pilot scale in brine regions including Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni, and announced a $450 million funding commitment in 2022 to build commercial capacity. Its LiTAS solid-state platform and ion-selective membranes target both battery manufacturers and brine producers. EnergyX now positions itself across the lithium value chain in the Americas.

name: H2Pro
short_description: E-TAC electrolyzer that splits water into hydrogen at unprecedented efficiency.
why_relevant: Thermodynamically clever two-step water splitting enables cheap green H2.
history: H2Pro was founded in 2019 as a spinoff from Technion to commercialize the E-TAC electrolysis cycle, a two-step method that decouples hydrogen and oxygen production to avoid the efficiency ceiling of conventional electrolyzers. The company raised a $79 million Series B in 2022 from investors including Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Hyundai and bp. It validated kilowatt-scale prototypes and moved toward multi-hundred-kilowatt stack demonstrations. H2Pro aims to produce green hydrogen at lower cost by eliminating membranes and separators from the water-splitting process entirely.

name: Bloom Energy
short_description: Manufactures solid oxide fuel cells generating on-site clean power.
why_relevant: NYSE-listed generator of always-on clean power for data centers.
history: Bloom Energy was founded in 2001 by former NASA scientist K.R. Sridhar to convert his Mars mission life-support research into solid oxide fuel cells. The company went public on the NYSE in 2018, and its boxed 'Energy Server' units found a market among businesses and utilities seeking on-site clean power. Bloom later expanded into electrolyzers and hydrogen production, signing large procurement agreements with data-center and industrial customers. By 2024 the company was generating record revenue and shipping its cells across the United States despite ongoing profitability challenges.

name: Betavolt
short_description: Develops betavoltaic atomic batteries that deliver power for decades.
why_relevant: Microwatt power for decades could power sensors without any recharge.
history: Betavolt was founded in 2021 in Beijing to commercialize betavoltaic power sources that convert radioactive decay directly into electricity. In early 2024 the company unveiled the BV100, a coin-sized battery using nickel-63 that can deliver power for decades, targeting sensors and small electronics. Betavolt said it plans to scale production and later introduce higher-power versions such as the BV200 for applications including medical implants and remote monitoring devices. The technology remains at low microwatt output but has drawn global attention for its potential to eliminate batteries and recharging in long-lifetime devices.

name: Ion Storage Systems
short_description: Develops high-density, anode-free solid-state ceramic batteries.
why_relevant: Doubles energy density while removing flammable liquid electrolyte.
history: Ion Storage Systems spun out of the University of Maryland in 2018 to develop anode-free, high-density ceramic batteries that operate at room temperature. The company won early government support from ARPA-E and the Department of Defense for its dense multilayer cells. In 2024 it raised tens of millions of dollars, including investment from TE Connectivity, to install automated assembly lines. It targets applications from consumer electronics to defense and eventually electric vehicles, claiming roughly twice the energy density of conventional cells without flammable liquid electrolyte.

name: Factorial Energy
short_description: Lot hundreds of solid-state cells for automotive qualification.
why_relevant: Path to 400 Wh/kg cells validated on production vehicle lines.
history: Factorial Energy was founded in 2019 to bring sulfide-based solid-state cells to scale, quickly earning one of the sector's largest early commitments when Daimler invested $200 million in 2020. A pilot plant opened in 2022, and in 2023 the company announced its Solstice platform licensed by Hyundai, Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz and LG Energy Solution. Factorial shipped hundreds of 40 Ah cells and later 100 Ah A-samples for customer qualification, targeting 400 Wh/kg performance. It is among the leaders able to run solid-state production on conventional lithiation equipment.

name: Our Next Energy (ONE)
short_description: Builds dual-chemistry battery packs with LFP and anode-free ranges.
why_relevant: Made one of the first electric 'mining van' batteries on US soil.
history: Our Next Energy (ONE) was founded in 2020 by Mujeeb Ijaz, the former Apple and A123 Systems executive, to pair LFP cells with high-range packs. The company made its public mark in 2022 with the Gemini 1,000-mile battery, followed by the Aries LFP line validated by BMW for its i7 prototype. ONE announced a $201.7 million US manufacturing project in Michigan and delivered one of the first battery-electric mining vans in the US. After funding headwinds in 2024, the company restructured around its core LFP business while keeping the Gemini advancement program.

name: FREYR Battery
short_description: Builds clean battery factories using 24M semi-solid cells in the UK and US.
why_relevant: Fast solvent-free production could make regional batteries competitive.
history: FREYR Battery was founded in Norway in 2018 as a licensed GigaFactory partner of 24M Technologies, aiming to manufacture cheaper, solvent-free cells from renewable power. The company listed on the NYSE in 2021, raising nearly one billion dollars for a planned plant in Mo i Rana and later projects in the UK and United States. After strategic reviews, FREYR shifted focus to US manufacturing and expanded into adjacent opportunities, securing offtake and financing frameworks around grid-scale and industrial cell output rather than a single large factory.

name: Powin Energy
short_description: One of the largest global integrators of grid battery energy storage systems.
why_relevant: The integrator adding the most grid storage capacity worldwide.
history: Powin Energy was founded in 2011 in Oregon and grew from small-scale demonstrators into one of the world's largest integrators of grid battery energy storage systems. Its proprietary StackOS platform manages safety, controls and digital optimization across containerized BESS deployments. By 2022 the company claimed the title of leading global integrator on contracted capacity and announced projects with utilities across North America, Asia and Australia. Powin continues expanding its manufacturing partnerships and software offering to support multi-gigawatt storage pipelines.

name: Fluence
short_description: Siemens/AES energy storage platform operating across global grids.
why_relevant: Trusted turnkey storage for utilities from the US to the Middle East.
history: Fluence was formed in 2018 as a joint venture between Siemens and AES to supply grid-scale storage and bidding software globally, drawing on AES's fleet of installed storage. The company added edge-of-grid software through acquisitions and attracted the Qatar Investment Authority as an anchor investor. Fluence went public on NASDAQ in 2022, when it already had the largest contracted pipeline in the industry. It has since deployed gigawatt-hours of systems across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, while launching products such as the sixth-generation Gridstack.

name: ESS Inc
short_description: Makes long-duration iron-flow batteries for renewables plus storage.
why_relevant: Abundant, safe materials for 8-to-12-hour stationary storage.
history: ESS Inc was founded in 2011 in Wilsonville, Oregon to develop long-duration iron-flow batteries built around an inexpensive, non-flammable iron-salt electrolyte. The company listed on the NYSE in 2021 via SPAC, raising capital to industrialize its technology, and has since deployed megawatt-scale systems in the United States, Australia and Europe. Customers such as Sacramento Municipal Utility District and SB Energy selected ESS for multi-hour renewable firming. Its Energy Center product line is backed by a 25-year design life with unlimited cycling of the active electrolyte.

name: Invinity Energy
short_description: Builds utility-scale vanadium flow batteries with unlimited cycling.
why_relevant: Deployed dual 10 MWh systems proving flow batteries at grid scale.
history: Invinity Energy Systems was formed in 2018 through the merger of UK-based redT Energy and Canadian vanadium-flow pioneer Avalon Battery. The combined company assumed listing on London's AIM and built utility-scale vanadium redox flow systems known for unlimited cycling. Its systems were deployed at Oxford Energy Superhub and later in Australia, where dual 10 MWh installations for remote microgrids broke new ground. With production in the UK and investment from strategic partners, Invinity continues to grow its pipeline for multi-hour storage.

name: Redflow
short_description: Deploys zinc-bromine flow batteries for tough, remote telecom load profiles.
why_relevant: Full daily cycling with no degradation in high-heat environments.
history: Redflow was founded in Brisbane in 2005 and became one of the first companies to commercialize zinc-bromine flow batteries, an abundant-material chemistry suited to hard, remote and cyclic loads. It listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in 2010 and supplied telecom sites across Australia, South Africa and the Philippines without the thermal failure modes of lithium. The company evolved from smaller zinc-bromine modules toward containerized ZBB systems. After capital restructurings, Redflow remains focused on long-duration cycling in off-grid and high-temperature environments.

name: Gravitricity
short_description: Lifts heavy weights to store grid energy without rare materials.
why_relevant: Uses mine shafts for decades of storage with zero circular battery materials.
history: Gravitricity was founded in Edinburgh in 2019 to store energy by raising and lowering massive weights in deep shafts, using gravity instead of battery chemistry. A 250 kW demonstrator in Leith validated the concept in 2021, and partnerships with ABB and with mining groups explored reusing disused mine shafts as storage sites. Following tests in the Czech Republic, the company raised further funding and appointed new leadership to pursue first commercial projects. Gravitricity positions itself as a long-life, round-trip storage option with no rare or circular materials.

name: Energy Vault
short_description: Builds gravity and kinetic storage plus software to balance grids.
why_relevant: First gravity-storage systems connected to commercial grids.
history: Energy Vault was founded in 2017 by Robert Piconi and Andrea Pedretti to build grid storage from gravity and kinetic techniques. The company gained global attention with its crane-based tower designs, then moved to the EVx modular composite-block architecture. It went public on the NYSE in 2022 through a SPAC merger and signed early agreements in Europe, China and the US. A first commercial EVx system became operational in Rudong, China. Energy Vault later expanded into utility-scale BESS hybrid plants and a cement-like eco-friendly building block line.

name: Hydrostor
short_description: Long-duration compressed air energy storage in underground caverns.
why_relevant: Multi-hundred MWh advanced CAES plants with no lithium demands.
history: Hydrostor was founded in Toronto in 2010 to commercialize advanced compressed-air energy storage (A-CAES) in underground caverns using off-the-shelf turbomachinery. The company completed a demonstration plant in Goderich, Ontario, and raised a $250 million growth round in 2022 backed by investors including Goldman Sachs and Canada Pension Plan. It advanced permitting for multi-hundred-MWh projects in New South Wales, Australia and a 500 MW project in California. Hydrostor's model pairs lower-cost air compression with heat recovery to deliver 8-hour-plus storage without lithium.

name: Ampcera
short_description: Develops sulfide solid electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries.
why_relevant: Manufactured electrolyte needed to make solid-state cells producible.
history: Ampcera was founded in 2016 in Tucson, Arizona to supply sulfide and chloride solid electrolytes, the materials many solid-state cell makers consider the enabling bottleneck. It won early US research awards and later scaled its electrolyte powder manufacturing, shipping material to cell development partners. In 2024 Ampcera expanded into silicon anode development and received further awards for solid-state prototype work including with the US Army. The company positions itself as a materials platform provider able to produce electrolyte at the tonne scale needed for pilot and future mass production.

name: Nanotech Energy
short_description: Makes graphene supercapacitors and non-flammable electrolyte batteries.
why_relevant: Fire-safe batteries for aviation and instant-power supercapacitor banks.
history: Nanotech Energy was founded in 2012 in California to commercialize graphene batteries and supercapacitors developed at UCLA. The company developed a fire-safe electrolyte and later acquired battery pack maker Voltaplex to control its supply chain. In 2023 Nanotech opened a large-format battery manufacturing facility in Compton, California, targeting aviation, defense and high-performance applications that value non-flammability. Its graphene-based electrodes also underpin instant-power supercapacitor banks, and the company continues scaling production with support from private and public financing.

name: SES AI
short_description: Develops hybrid lithium-metal cells with real-time AI monitoring.
why_relevant: First automotive-qualified Li-metal cells announced for electric aircraft and EVs.
history: SES AI was founded in 2012 as SolidEnergy Systems, growing from MIT research into a hybrid lithium-metal battery developer, and went public on the NYSE in 2021 via SPAC under the ticker SES. The company built a robust partner ecosystem with GM, Honda, Hyundai and Geely through its Apollo program and opened a lithium-metal facility in Shanghai. SES shipped B-samples of its automotive lithium-metal cells in 2024 and developed the Avatar AI software platform that monitors cell health in real time. It is now targeting both electric vehicles and electric aviation.

name: Voltaiq
short_description: Software that aggregates battery test data to predict cell lifetime.
why_relevant: Standard analytics layer for most cell and pack engineering teams.
history: Voltaiq was founded in 2012 in Berkeley, California by battery scientists to create software that unifies test, manufacturing and field data across the battery lifecycle. Its platform aggregates data from cell design through deployed fleets, applying statistical models to predict lifetime and performance. The company grew through private funding and became a standard analytics layer for many cell and pack engineering teams, serving customers across EVs, consumer electronics and energy storage. Decades of accumulated test data give Voltaiq a benchmarking edge for cross-cell comparison and failure prediction.

name: Twaice
short_description: Digital twin software modeling EV and energy battery health.
why_relevant: Used by OEMs to monetize battery health across the fleet lifecycle.
history: Twaice was founded in 2018 in Munich as a spinout of the Technical University of Munich to create digital twins of lithium-ion batteries. Its software simulates and predicts state-of-health, enabling OEMs and fleet operators to optimize warranties, second-life use and resale value. The company raised successive funding rounds from European investors and expanded into analytics for energy storage systems. Twaice now serves manufacturers and fleet managers worldwide, turning battery data into actionable decisions over the full asset lifecycle.
